Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)  
- Assessment consistent with olecranon bursitis: Recent onset swelling and mild warmth localized to left elbow without pain or loss of function, no trauma history, dry skin over site; clinical impression by GP supports diagnosis (High likelihood)  
- Septic bursitis: Considered less likely; no redness, severe pain, or systemic symptoms; mild discomfort near swelling present (Medium likelihood)  
- Gout or crystal arthropathy: Possible given new joint swelling; no severe pain or redness; blood tests planned to rule out (Medium likelihood)  
- Rheumatologic inflammatory arthritis (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis): Unlikely given no systemic symptoms, no other joint involvement, and no known family history; blood tests arranged for screening (Low to Medium likelihood)  

Management Plan  
- Initiate oral ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food; stop if heartburn occurs  
- Arrange and send blood test forms for inflammatory markers, autoimmune antibodies, infection screen, and gout profile to patient’s home with instructions  
- Follow-up appointment to review blood test results and clinical status; can be telehealth or face-to-face based on patient preference  
- Advise patient to seek urgent assessment if elbow becomes red, very painful, or swelling worsens, indicating possible infection
